slides.transcript:
Start with the front panel. IceCube has sixty-four O S F P connectors. So how can the switch offer a hundred and twenty-eight eight-hundred-gigabit Ethernet interfaces?

Follow one transmit signal. It starts at the switch ASIC, beneath the cold plate on the Switch Main Board. The signal travels electrically over high-speed flyover cables to a Physical Interface Card. At the faceplate, the pluggable module converts the electrical signal to light and sends it out through fiber.

Zoom in on one connector. With Meta's dual eight-hundred-gigabit module, one connector carries two independent eight-hundred-gigabit Ethernet interfaces. Each of the two interface cards carries thirty-two connectors. Multiply sixty-four by two by eight hundred gigabits per second. That's one hundred and two point four terabits per second.

The specification also lists five hundred and twelve two-hundred-gigabit Ethernet interfaces. That's the same total capacity at a different interface rate. When reading a port count, ask whether it describes the faceplate or the configured interfaces.

slides.subtitle: The Broadcom Tomahawk6C reference uses flyover cables. Meta’s IceCube-N preview uses NVIDIA Spectrum-6 and routes its 212G PAM4 signals on the PCB.
slides.transcript:
In the top view, orient yourself with the front on the left. The switch ASIC sits under the large cold plate in the center. Its serializer and deserializer, called SerDes, drive high-speed electrical signals toward the front. The yellow cable assemblies are the electrical flyover path. They carry those signals inside the chassis to the Physical Interface Cards and the O S F P connectors.

The design specification describes the IceCube variant based on Broadcom’s Tomahawk six C. Meta also announced a variant based on Nvidia’s Spectrum six. The signal path here follows the Broadcom-based design described in the O C P specification.

The specification calls the board design PHY-less. In this path, the host signal reaches the pluggable module without going through a separate board-level PHY chip. The optical module changes the outgoing electrical signal into light. In the other direction, the module receives light and converts it back to an electrical signal for the switch.

questions.prompt: Where does an outgoing electrical signal become optical?

choices.feedback_incorrect: The SerDes launches the electrical host signal. Look farther along the path for conversion into light.
The flyover cable carries the host signal electrically to the front-panel interface.
The connector interfaces to the module. Optical conversion takes place in the module.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. The optical module transmits onto fiber.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Trace the electrical path through the connector and into the module.

questions.prompt: All 64 OSFP openings hold dual-800G modules. Which statements are true?

choices.text: The faceplate still has 64 physical OSFP connectors.
Each installed module exposes one 800GbE interface.
The QSFP28 management connector contributes to the 128 interfaces.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Each of the 64 modules provides two 800GbE interfaces.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Count the modules against the physical openings. Then count two 800GbE interfaces per dual-800G module.

slides.transcript:
IceCube slides into a two Open Unit space in an Open Rack version three High Power Rack. A canister adapter fits the switch to the rack. Here, the rack supplies power and connects the switch to the coolant loop.

Inside, liquid-cooled cold plates carry heat away from the switch ASIC and the O S F P optics. Follow the other path from the front of the switch to its rear fans. That airflow cools the microserver, the baseboard management controller, the power stages, the solid-state drive, and the Q S F P twenty-eight management module.

Now look directly at the rear. Coolant enters on your right through a blind-mate coupling. It returns on your left. The central connector mates to the rack's D C power busbar. Between the coolant couplings, four fans draw air through the chassis.

Back at the front, two optical form factors sit near each other. Which uses liquid cooling? The O S F P bank uses cold plates. The Q S F P twenty-eight depends on airflow.

slides.transcript:
At the front, several connections use the same R J forty-five shape. Read the label and match the connector to the job. The one-gigabit out-of-band Ethernet port provides platform management access to the microserver and the baseboard management controller. The serial console uses R S two thirty-two and connects to the B M C. The leak-sensing connection exchanges signals with the rack management controller.

The Q S F P twenty-eight connection is an Ethernet management path into the switch ASIC. Before you troubleshoot, decide which device owns what you’re trying to observe. For a fan fault, you want the platform management path to the microserver or B M C.

slides.title: Diagnose a cooling or fan issue
slides.subtitle: Submit an answer to both questions to continue. You can retry after feedback.

questions.prompt: Coolant is circulating, but front-to-back airflow falls. Which component depends on that airflow?

choices.feedback_incorrect: The switch ASIC is served by a liquid cold plate.
The populated OSFP optics are served by liquid cold plates.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. The E1.S drive relies on front-to-back airflow.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Separate the liquid-cooled ASIC and OSFP bank from the air-cooled components.

questions.prompt: A rear fan drops below its RPM threshold. Which statements guide your first review?

choices.text: Use RJ45 OOB Ethernet for platform management.
The ASIC’s QSFP28 management link is the platform fan-management path.
The microserver runs the fan-speed algorithm.
The fan trays are field-replaceable at the rear.
The rack controller determines each fan’s speed.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Use platform management, trace fan speed to the microserver, and find the tray at the rear.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Keep access, control, and physical service separate. Use the platform’s out-of-band management connection, the microserver’s fan control, and the rear fan trays.

lms_catalog.short_description: Trace IceCube’s ASIC-to-optics path, then explore its Ethernet interfaces, hybrid cooling, and field service.
lms_catalog.overview: Explore Meta’s 102.4 Tb/s IceCube Ethernet switch from its front-panel connectors to its ORv3 HPRv1 power and cooling interfaces. Practice reading the chassis, interpreting port counts, and locating management and service points.

modules.summary: Follow an electrical transmit signal to the pluggable optics. Interpret two system configurations and tell physical connectors from logical Ethernet interfaces.
Locate the ORv3 HPRv1 rack connections, trace two cooling paths, and diagnose a slow fan using IceCube’s hardware management architecture.

term_glossary.tooltip: Octal Small Form Factor Pluggable. The front-panel connector and pluggable module follow this form factor.
Serializer/deserializer. This circuit drives and receives high-speed serial electrical lane signals.
Blind-mate quick-connect. The rear liquid coupling mates to its rack-side connection as the chassis seats.
IceCube’s management split. The BMC handles critical functions such as power-on and recovery. The microserver handles sensors and fan-speed control.
